# SOP-P1-L2-01 Line startup - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-009, SB-1008, SB-1020

1. Purpose and scope
1.1 Purpose: Define required steps to perform safe, consistent startup of the Ring Rolling line on P1-L2, including mechanical, electrical, lubrication and heat-treat readiness checks prior to production.
1.2 Scope: Applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance staff responsible for EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03.

2. Background and rationale
2.1 Background: The Ring Rolling line has tight interdependencies between the induction heater, ring rolling mill, and the heat-treat furnace. Improper sequence or overlooked readiness items can cause part quality escapes, equipment damage, or personnel hazards.
2.2 Rationale: This procedure sequences checks to verify mechanical clearances, lubrication, control interlocks, and quench timing before introducing parts. The defined steps reduce risk of rework and unscheduled downtime. See ECN-2026-009 for recent control updates and SB-1008 and SB-1020 for safety bulletins that affect startup practices.

3. Preconditions (required conditions before initiating startup)
3.1 Subject matter experts: Operator and one maintenance technician assigned and present.
3.2 Permits: Any applicable lockout/tagout cleared, and permit documentation reviewed per SB-1008.
3.3 Housekeeping: Work area around EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 is free of loose materials and obstructions.
3.4 Controls: PLC and HMI panels are powered, connected to plant network, and show normal boot without active alarms.
3.5 Consumables: Verify lubricant availability; the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is CFW-LUB-788. Verify quench media and quench tank readiness for EQ-P1-L2-HT03. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds.

4. Required personal protective equipment (PPE)
4.1 Minimum PPE for personnel during startup: safety glasses, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, and flame-resistant clothing where directed by SB-1020. Additional PPE as directed by the site safety officer for specific tasks such as handling hot billets.

5. Procedure — numbered steps
5.1 Pre-start verification
5.1.1 Confirm preconditions in section 3 are met.
5.1.2 Notify line control and adjacent work centers that startup is commencing; obtain verbal acknowledgement.

5.2 Mechanical and safety checks
5.2.1 Visual inspect machine guards on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 for secure fasteners and intact interlock switches.
5.2.2 Verify all access doors on EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 close and lock; confirm interlock status on HMI.
5.2.3 Inspect quench tank area for water level, flow indicators, and return lines for obstructions. Confirm emergency stop circuits are functional.

5.3 Lubrication and consumables
5.3.1 Replenish lubrication points for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 per lubrication map. For EQ-P1-L2-IH02 confirm lubricant match; the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is CFW-LUB-788.
5.3.2 Record batch or lot number of lubricant used in the startup log.

5.4 Electrical and controls
5.4.1 Release local lockouts and perform controlled energization of drive systems. Confirm fault logs clear and baseline alarm set recorded.
5.4.2 Perform control homing routines from HMI and validate interlock logic by simulating a safe interruption.

5.5 Heat-treat furnace staging
5.5.1 With the furnace at idle, verify sensors and thermocouples are reporting and are within operational status on the HMI.
5.5.2 Confirm quench pump primed and flow meters indicate flow. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. Verify controller timing parameter matches this value.

5.6 Dry run and coupling checks
5.6.1 Run the line in dry-run mode without billets to verify synchronization between EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Observe for abnormal vibration, noise, or motion.
5.6.2 If any abnormal condition is detected, stop the line and document observations, reference SB-1008 for safety reporting, and engage maintenance.

5.7 First billet introduction
5.7.1 Introduce a single sacrificial billet with monitoring by the operator and technician. Observe induction heating behavior, roll engagement, and quench timing.
5.7.2 Collect dimensional samples and surface quality checks for immediate evaluation. If the part fails acceptance, halt production and follow ECN-2026-009 for corrective engineering action.

6. Examples and acceptance criteria
6.1 Example observation: If induction heater shows uneven heating zones, document heater zone current imbalance in the startup log and tag for corrective maintenance. Reference SB-1020 for handling instructions of hot parts.
6.2 Acceptance is defined by equipment running without alarms, synchronization achieved in dry-run, lubricant batch recorded, and quench timing verified against the required setting.

7. Records to keep
7.1 Startup log: operator name, technician name, line identifier P1-L2, equipment IDs EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03, lubricant part number used, and any noted observations.
7.2 Alarm and fault snapshot: save PLC/HMI logs for the startup interval and attach to the startup log.
7.3 Sample inspection report: include dimensional and visual inspection records for the first production pieces and any sacrificial billet results.
7.4 Maintenance tags and corrective actions: file per ECN-2026-009 if adjustments or repairs are required.

8. Sign-off
8.1 Operator sign-off: operator verifies all steps completed and initial here.
8.2 Lead technician sign-off: lead technician verifies mechanical and lubrication readiness and initial here.
8.3 Production supervisor sign-off: production supervisor approves line for production and initial here.

9. References
9.1 ECN-2026-009
9.2 SB-1008
9.3 SB-1020

Notes: Follow all site safety policies and document deviations from this SOP in the startup log.
